home    about    brands    Contact    Visit our Store                Visit our Store               Home    About    Brands    Contact    Visit our Store           © 2026 All Rights Reserved Future Art Broadcast Trading LLC              About Us    Future Art Broadcast Trading LLC was founded in Baghdad in 1994 and has amassed over 30 years of expertise in the broadcast, cinema, and media industry. Over the decades, we have not only kept pace with the region’s rapid technological advancements but have also played a key role in driving innovation. Rather than merely adopting global developments, we have actively contributed to shaping the media industry in the Middle East and Africa, delivering solutions that meet the highest international standards while addressing the region’s unique needs.  As part of our expansion strategy, we established our company in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, in 2006, enabling us to extend our services across the Middle East and Africa. Beyond our main locations, we have company representatives in several neighboring countries and are actively pursuing further expansion, where we aim to open new branches to strengthen our presence and serve a broader network of clients.  At Future Art, we are one of the leading companies specializing in audio-video solutions in the Middle East. With decades of experience, we have established ourselves as a key player in the industry, providing cutting-edge technology and seamless integration services. We proudly operate the largest showrooms in Dubai and Baghdad, where we showcase a diverse range of products from over 60 globally recognized brands, for which we serve as the official distributor. Our extensive product portfolio covers broadcast, cinema, professional audio equipment, ensuring that media professionals have access to the latest innovations in the field.  Our expertise extends far beyond product sales. We specialize in system integration, offering fully customized solutions in broadcast and media technology. Our services include the establishment of complete television stations, the design and implementation of advanced studios, and the integration of mobile production units, including outside broadcast (OB) vans. Additionally, we provide comprehensive solutions for radio broadcasting, equipping stations with the latest transmission and audio processing technologies. In the cinema industry, we deliver high-end projection and digital display solutions, along with advanced media storage and data transmission systems that optimize workflow efficiency and content management.  What truly sets Future Art apart is our team of highly skilled and certified engineers, who have been trained and accredited by the world's leading technology providers. With specialized expertise across various domains, our engineers are dedicated to delivering technical support, maintenance, and system optimization services to ensure that our clients' operations run smoothly and efficiently. Whether it’s integrating complex broadcast systems, upgrading production facilities, or providing post-sales support, we remain committed to offering state-of-the-art equipment, tailored solutions, and unparalleled engineering expertise.  By combining innovation, technical excellence, and a commitment to customer satisfaction, we continue to empower media professionals across the Middle East and Africa with the tools and technologies they need to succeed in an ever-evolving industry.            Vision   Our vision is to deliver the latest advancements in broadcast, cinema, and media technology to our clients, providing creators with the tools they need to turn their ideas into reality—at the most competitive prices.        Mission   We empower media professionals by providing broadcast, cinema, and media technology solutions. As an authorized representor of leading global brands, we provide state-of-the-art products, seamless system integration, and exceptional after-sales support. Our commitment is to innovation, efficiency, and customer satisfaction, ensuring that our clients achieve excellence in content creation, production, and broadcasting.           Interested? title: Breakcorelist – some suggestions and writings for those interested in breakcore
content: Skip to content     Breakcorelist  some suggestions and writings for those interested in breakcore     Menu  Home  About Breakcorelist  Contact          THE BEGINNER’S GUIDE TO BREAKCORE : Celebrating 30 years of Breakcore (1992-2022)       June 20, 2017 December 17, 2022 ~ breakcorelist    THE BEGINNER’S GUIDE TO BREAKCORE (AND FURTHER SUGGESTED LISTENING): Compiled by Boris Otterdam (and various others in the worldwide breakcore scene) UPDATED FOR THE 30TH ANNIVERSARY OF BREAKCORE IN JUNE 2022.  Original intro written June 21st 2017.  A list of breakcore records, EPs, tapes and singles (UPDATED June 2022)  For the last few years, there’s been people new to the genre of breakcore, asking “what it is?” or “what can you recommend me?” on Facebook groups, forums and other social media.  Originally. I set out to make a short list to recommend to a friend, but it occurred to me that there was almost no resource for people wanting to investigate this music, aside from the giant debate heavy forums that are social media, Some new fans and producers that I had met, had told me that they found “the same thing” over and over and wanted to find something else.  In the 30 years since breakcore was birthed almost at the same time in different locations all over the world. It has gone through a variety of changes. Many of these changes have been controversial among those who were a part of the original inception and subsequent scenes it inhabited. Some have been controversial among the new breed of producers and DJs that have come to the forefront in the past decade.  Past, present and future generations, rarely seeing eye to eye.  The more I thought about the concept of making a list of prominent breakcore releases. The more it became pointless to only list a few.  If I only included the seminal well known (well known among breakcore scenes not the bulk of the world’s population) releases and labels – I would not be able to include the hidden underground gems that had small press runs or were only available on cassette. If I only included the original definitions of the breakcore sound. I would ostracize those who are only interested in what it sounds like now. If I only included the current incarnation. I would ostracize many of the old school producers and fans of the early sounds.  In the end, I decided to include it all.  So, I asked producers, DJs, fans and followers.  Some that were pioneers of the movement from the very beginning, some that were around for the old school, some that were a part of the second wave, some that were a part of the popmash years and finally those who have been a part of it in the last decade or so. Many of these people were adamant that non-breakcore releases should also be included if they were deemed to be a major influence on other producers. So although there are literally thousands of jungle, breakbeat, IDM, drum n bass and hardcore records I could choose from there. I chose sparingly and only included them if they had a sizeable influence on the sound.  Using these suggestions, my own collection and a lot of research. I’ve come up with a list of releases that cover all bases. It’s not an ultimate list. It’s an answer to the question “What’s some good breakcore?” or “What’s good that’s like breakcore?”  In making this list. I tried to be bipartisan. But having been promoting breakcore for 24 years. I decided to only include releases I heard and enjoyed myself and thought were worth recommending.  So what you have is a list of seminal and essential releases alongside personal recommendations, noteworthy influential records, overlooked gems, forgotten greats and current trailblazers.  A final list compiled with suggestions from myself, world famous producers, unknown producers and lovers and obsessives of the breakcore ideology and sound…  ..just like me.  To truly experience breakcore best, requires taking in more than one interpretation than just the dominant scenes in the USA, UK and Europe. Scenes in places like Spain, Australia, Russia, Japan and South America to name a few. All harbor breakcore scenes with incredible and unique takes on the sound. Where possible, I have tried to include a large cross section of various scenes. Even if it’s only one or two releases.  Breakcore is a highly addictive and passionate style of predominantly breakbeat driven techno. It’s not owned by any one scene and once it’s out there. It inspires, revolts, entertains and polarizes audiences everywhere. There will always be debate over what it is, where it’s been, where it is and where it’s going but it’s an entity of it’s own and the path it chooses can’t be altered. You can complain about where it’s going but you can’t stop it. You just have to accept that.  Despite what Wikipedia or online experts would have you believe. It’s not as easily definable as some might like to think. It IS NOT defined by amen breaks – or even breaks at all. In compiling this list, I have included many contributions

Skip to content     Breakcorelist  some suggestions and writings for those interested in breakcore     Menu  Home  About Breakcorelist  Contact         Author: breakcorelist Boris Otterdam is a West Australian born electronic music producer, label manager, promoter and radio show host.
Beginning in 1998 as a promoter for the Perth punk rock scene, Boris began experimenting with analogue noise and soundscapes as a member of noise band "Analogue Seaotter"
After Analogue Seaotter disbanded he released a limited cassette as "Boris Otterdam" before co-founding Perth's first breakcore/experimental label 8-Bit Recordings with The Last Ninja and Deadcode in 2000.
8-Bit Recordings was the first label of it's kind in Western Australia and was responsible for organizing the first ever breakcore shows in Western Australia.
Boris has self published zines, written for and assisted in designing local music websites, blogs and publications, released cassette compilations, played in and collaborated with bands and producers, organized and promoted punk rock, noise, breakcore, hardcore, goth and indie shows in Perth and Melbourne as well as hosted and co-hosted the final incarnation of System Corrupt Radio Show on 2serfm Sydney, Illegal Frequencies on 2serfm Sydney, Illegal Frequencies and Fuck You and Yours on 2serfm Sydney and RRRfm Melbourne from 2004-2013.

As of 2015 he is based in Tweed Heads on The Gold Coast where he runs Australian label "Ende Records" and freelance writes for various online blogs.

As well as Noistruct, Boris produces extreme noise and dark ambient soundscapes as Mandark, drum n bass and jungle as Holt, 4/4 experimental, acid and minimal techno as Notex, distorted house and dirty disco as Basic Bitch and is one half of electronic duo "Midusa"     THE BEGINNER’S GUIDE TO BREAKCORE : Celebrating 30 years of Breakcore (1992-2022)       June 20, 2017 December 17, 2022 ~ breakcorelist    THE BEGINNER’S GUIDE TO BREAKCORE (AND FURTHER SUGGESTED LISTENING): Compiled by Boris Otterdam (and various others in the worldwide breakcore scene) UPDATED FOR THE 30TH ANNIVERSARY OF BREAKCORE IN JUNE 2022.
